chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Alwan narrated from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Paradise is forbidden to three: to the one who puts others under obligation, to the backbiter, and to the habitual drinker of wine.'

key_terms.الْمُنَّانِ: The one who puts others under obligation by reminding them of favors

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people forbidden from Paradise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the lineage of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, identifies three spiritual impediments to Paradise: the Munan (who nullifies charity by reminding recipients of favors), the Mughibah (who engages in backbiting), and the Mudmin al-Khamr (the habitual drinker). In Shia tradition, these traits represent internal corruption of character that obstructs divine grace, with 'Mudmin' specifically denoting consistent, unrepentant consumption rather than occasional use.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 17.Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān narrated from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his fathers, from ʿAlī (a) who said, “
The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said, ‘Paradise is forbidden to three: to the one who puts others under obligation, to the one who backbites, and to the one who is a habitual drinker.’”
